facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Describes itself as 'a buyer-led evaluation platform for security tools': a ranked shortlist no vendor can pay to influence, then a private evaluation; free for security teams.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Three acts: a conversational AI briefing scopes the problem; a deterministic scoring engine ranks the catalogue into a shortlist with reasons; a private workspace runs the evaluation on criteria weighted before any vendor is invited.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: 'AI conducts the briefing; it does not rank vendors, and vendors cannot pay for placement.'

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Scores rest on what vendors can prove, not what they promise; if a vendor has not shared the data, the buyer sees that, and every product ruled out has a reason.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Its directory lists 3,000+ security products from 1,000+ vendors across 60+ categories, including AI runtime and agent security, AI-SPM and agentic SOC.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: It offers an MCP server so Claude or ChatGPT can query its vendor facts.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Vendors can claim their profile and take part in evaluations.

told: Its card says: 'Less noise. Better cybersecurity matches. Connecting cybersecurity buyers and vendors.'
It is a cybersecurity startup in vendor management, free for buyers.
domain_note: No domain was given. picari.ai (picari.io redirects to it) matches the card's words: a platform connecting cybersecurity buyers and vendors, free for buyers. The company has not confirmed it yet.

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: Picari ranks security tools on what vendors can prove. GAMMA-Ray rates agentic products on public evidence against published standards, with every claim linked to its source and a trust level per fact. For the AI and agent security categories in Picari's directory, that is a second, evidence-graded view a buyer can read: an opinion without confrontation.

mandate.text: For the agentic tools in its catalogue: what each product says its agents do, written down per configuration, as GAMMA-Ray does today.

reach.text: What those agents can reach (connectors, permissions, tools), rated from public evidence and, with the vendor, measured.

gap.text: Its own principle, 'if a vendor hasn't shared the data, you'll know', is the same as GAMMA-Ray's 'not yet evidenced'. The gap between claim and evidence is what both make visible.

together.label: Our suggestions. Nothing here is agreed.

items.title: Run GAMMA-Ray on the catalogue
items.text: Seven or eight standards with specific requirements give an opinion without confrontation: each product's card links every level to public evidence (Dinis's first point).

items.title: Rank data by assurance level
items.text: Scraped or public, vendor-commented, customer opinion, regulator opinion: FACT-Ray already grades each fact by who says it and how firmly it is recorded (Dinis's second point).

items.title: Openness against pay-to-play
items.text: Public reviews and on-record evidence, with a graph linking every claim to its evidence, as PrompTugal and GAMMA-Ray publish (Dinis's third point).

items.title: Signed identities and versioned vaults
items.text: A key pair for every party and agent, and SGit vaults for versioned, signed data (Dinis's fourth point).

items.title: Trials and paid evaluations
items.text: Low-commitment trials for vendors and paid evaluation for buyers (Dinis's fifth point).
